newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian royalists seek replacement for Ranariddh.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian royalists seek replacement for Ranariddh.

text.p: A senior member of Cambodia's ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's party said on Friday it was time to seek a replacement for Ranariddh because of political realities.

"How can we organise a resistance (movement)? The situation is very different than previous years," said Loy Sim Chheang, secretary general of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and first vice president of the parliament. "We need to be flexible."
He said FUNCINPEC still existed and was preparing to ask Ranariddh to name a replacement as party president. The government was also taking steps to name a new first prime minister, he said.

Loy Sim Chheang was speaking to reporters before convening the first meeting of the permanent standing committee of the National Assembly since powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's forces toppled Ranariddh from power at the weekend.
He said royalists could no longer count on the type of regional support that enabled them to oppose Hun Sen's Hanoi-backed government in the 1980s.
Ranariddh has accused Hun Sen of staging a coup, but Hun Sen has denied the charge and said he would keep Cambodia's coalition government intact, although without Ranariddh.

Top candidates for the first prime minister slot are co-Defence Minister Tea Chamrath and Ton Chhay, a general in the armed forces and leader of a dissident group of FUNCINPEC officials that broke with Ranariddh in April.
"It's better to install Ton Chhay or Tea Chamrath because they are high-level commanders and they can control the military," Loy Sim Chheang said.
Tea Chamrath has said he would consider the job while Ton Chhay, who returned from a trip abroad on Friday, would only say he had come back to strengthen the FUNCINPEC party.

Officials who attended Friday's national assembly meeting said they had a full quorum of the 12-member group, but that at least four members of parliament who fled the country had been replaced in order to convene the committee.

At least 12 FUNCINPEC national assembly members have left Cambodia in the wake of Ranariddh's ouster and the subsequent killing of a senior party member and the suspected death of another FUNCINPEC official.
Standing committee officials said they had discussed the safety of remaining FUNCINPEC members at their meeting, which Loy Sim Chheang said was a party priority.
Most FUNCINPEC officials who have not left Cambodia have fallen in line with the new government, analysts said.
The National Assembly, previously deadlocked over rifts within FUNCINPEC, is expected to reconvene within two weeks, Loy Sim Chheang said.
